messages:
maya: Hey team — I've pasted the first-pass PRD for function-calling + structured-output validation for launch. Looking for: must-have acceptance criteria, clear error-handling semantics, and a prioritized edge-case list from eng/ML. TL;DR: customer asks around schema rejections breaking user flows; we need graceful degradation + observability. Link: https://redwood.internal/docs/prd/fcall-struct-validate (WIP)

alyssa: Reading now. Can we surface the key customer stories up top? enterprises care about deterministic failures (not silent truncation).

liam: Agree. From infra side: requirements we need to design for:
- clear API error codes (schema_mismatch, required_missing, invalid_type)
- lightweight schema validation path that runs pre-inference to avoid wasted GPU cycles
- fallback routing to text-only model when strict mode fails

sam: For ML/QoE: add a quality gate: if >X% of responses in production are downgraded to text fallback, auto-roll back to previous model. Also add a metric for "schema_conformance_rate" per-route.

maya: Good notes. Draft acceptance criteria suggestion: 
1) Happy path: model returns payload that validates against JSON Schema v7 -> API returns 200 + structured payload.
2) Schema mismatch: API returns 422 + error payload with {error_code, validation_errors[], model_output: optional_raw}.
3) Strict mode: customer can opt-in to "reject_on_schema_failure" -> 422 and no model_output returned.
4) Fallback mode (default for existing customers): when schema invalid, call fallback_text_model and return a best-effort text response + warning header.
5) Observability: logs for every validation failure including token counts, model name, and delta latency.

noah: A couple infra constraints: pre-validation means validating prompt + function spec (if using tool calls) for obvious mismatches, but we can't fully validate runtime outputs until model responds. Pre-validation ROI depends on how many rejects happen due to user prompt shape. Might be optional.

alyssa: Customer-driven asks: edge cases I've heard from support:
- missing required nested fields (e.g., address.street) when downstream systems expect them -> causes downstream 500s
- extra unknown fields getting dropped -> audit/compliance concerns
- incorrect enum values silently coerced -> data integrity issues
We need clear remediation steps for each in the PRD.

liam: Engineering proposals for error payload shape:
```
{
  "error_code": "schema_mismatch",
  "errors": [
    {"path":"$.user.address.street","reason":"missing_required"},
    {"path":"$.payment.method","reason":"invalid_enum","allowed":["card","ach"]}
  ],
  "model_id": "redwood-v1-128",
  "model_output_snippet": "{...}",
  "validation_version": "v1"
}
```
(replace with compact fields, but include path + reason for downstream mapping)

sam: For QA and acceptance tests, we should include synthetic prompts that trigger: nested-missing, extra-fields, invalid-type, large arrays (size limits), partial streaming outputs (stream cut mid-JSON). Streaming partial JSON is a big one — sometimes model streams a prefix and then a follow-up that completes. Validator needs to support streaming assembly window (e.g., 3s or 200 tokens).

maya: Good call. Add acceptance criteria for streaming: validator should allow an incremental-assembly timeout (configurable per-route). If assembly times out -> treat as partial output -> follow fallback/strict rules.

noah: Ops: add an SLI for "validation_latency_p50/p95" (should be <5ms ideally for pre-validate; post-validate adds to end-to-end latency budget). We'll also need retention of validation errors for 30d for audits. KMS keys/PII redaction must run before logs are persisted.

alyssa: Prioritization ask: We have three slices — core API shape + basic validation (MVP), strict mode & per-customer toggles (Phase 2), streaming assembly + canary rollback autopilot (Phase 3). Recommend MVP cover happy path + schema_mismatch semantics + observability.

liam: Implementation notes / edge tradeoffs:
- Running a fast JSON Schema validator in-process (wasm or native) vs remote validation service. In-process minimizes RPCs but increases memory in inference host. Remote service centralizes versions.
- Validation versioning: include validation_schema_id in response so we can trace regressions.

maya: Can someone sketch the minimal API surface for the PRD? e.g., request fields + response for success and failure.

liam: Minimal API sketch:
Request: POST /v1/generate
Headers: X-Redwood-Validation-Mode: strict|fallback
Body: {prompt: "..", function_schema: {...}}
Success 200: {status: "ok", output: {structured: {...}}, meta: {model: "...", validation_schema_id: "s123"}}
Fail 422: {status: "error", error_code: "schema_mismatch", errors: [...], meta: {...}}

sam: Add tests for partial stream: simulate chunked JSON with out-of-order braces and ensure assembly works. Also include golden prompts from 3 customers we anonymize.

maya: Action items:
- liam: mock API + error payload and perf estimates (due EOW)
- sam: test harness + rejection canary design (due next Tue)
- noah: ops retention + logging spec (due EOW)
- alyssa: update PRD with customer stories and prioritization (due Thu)

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: staging/validation-service v0.1 -> deploy at 2026-03-25T02:00Z (note: automated job)

alyssa: One more thing — acceptance criteria should include a manual runbook for support: how to interpret errors, how to toggle strict vs fallback per-customer, and rollback steps if canary thresholds exceed X%.

maya: Solid. I'll stitch this into the PRD and ping folks for a short 30m sync tomorrow. Thanks for the quick feedback :thumbsup:
